Synopsis:
    The Trump administration is set to approve expanded biofuel blending exemptions for small U.S. oil refineries, covering over 1.8 billion renewable fuel credits — roughly double the initially flagged volume. Key applicants include Marathon Petroleum and Chevron. Driven by efforts to suppress gasoline prices amid a U.S.-Iran conflict, the EPA may simultaneously reopen 2027 biofuel quotas to add ~500M+ credits to offset agricultural harm. The move reignites the structural tension between the refining industry and farm-state interests under the U.S. Renewable Fuel Standard.
